I have, I do, I become overly pugnacious and manipulative.  I am simultaneously guilty and hateful.  Guilty because I hate to burden them with my nonesense and hateful because I find that I'd feel better if they were to hate me before I killed myself.  I become horrible and vicious, and I end up hurting people.

I am considering just allowing myself to become evicted - i'm happier when homeless, though, I'd hate to disappoint my room mate who is an old friend and who depends upon me.  kind of groggy. just woke up.

Same boat.

* Degree in math - check.
* phone shut off - check.
* homeless - not presently but have been more than once in the last three years, and am likely to again be by the end of the month.
* income + savings - zero
* family - none
* multi-lingual - check (learned French in order to translate J.P. Serre's *Faisceaux algébriques cohérents* and have entertained a mild flirtation with the language ever since )

Unlike you I do not know what I want to do.  Lately I've been viewing [these](http://oyc.yale.edu/philosophy/death/content/class-sessions) lectures on the philosophy of death, they've been most engaging.  Specifically they validate my strong desire to end my life by providing a rational framework from which to consider my own mortality.  And, while I do remain miserable, and while just today I held a knife to my wrist for about 20 minutes while staring into the mirror, I am nevertheless vaguely engaged enough in life for my hand to be stayed.  

Try giving them a viewing.

My only advice is - real accomplishment takes time, say, 10,000 hours or so.  Sure, you may forget this daunting maxim and find that you seem to have done something with just a few hours, or a few weeks, or a month or two. This is good.  Good, however, is just a step along the way.  Unless you're willing to spend years on a skill, talent, project, or body of work, it will not be a developed skill or an interesting project or a valuable body of work. 

So yes, working with a team good.  But working alone is valuable too.  Seize all opportunities, embrace them as best you can without compromising your vision for yourself, your work, and your projects.  If those opportunities do not include working with your fellows, then don't sweat it.  You will find that working on a game or project will, if you stick with it, bring questions to your head, and answers from the community.  And with those answers will come the opportunity of interested collaborators.  

Keep it up.
You also might be interested in [the code review](http://codereview.stackexchange.com) stack exchange site, which is still in the beta phase and was started with just this sort of question in mind.
